answer: Quantifying Sybil resistance, collateral lockup via quadratic slashing erodes stake at n², forcing a fable of capital doubling for each marginal node; thus, attack cost scales super-linearly, where acquiring k nodes demands k² exposure, and any extracted value from consensus breach is dwarfed by the slashing sink. This thread of economic commitment ensures marginal costs exceed potential rents, as the sonnet of security dictates that protocol-level thresholds, set above the maximum extractable value, render even coordinated clusters unprofitable, guaranteeing equilibrium.
